newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares firmer at Friday lunchtime break.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares firmer at Friday lunchtime break.

text.p: Singapore shares were slightly firmer at Friday's lunchtime close with blue chip stocks gaining ground as investors jostled for key positions, dealers said.
"We're up but there are more traders than buyers out there. I think this is just positioning," one dealer said.
Stocks were unmoved by a speech from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that lifted currency futures on hopes that an expected U.S. interest rate hike might be postponed.
"The stock market has been anticipating a quarter point rise for a while and can handle it," one broker said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index rose 5.22 to 2,064.60.

The morning session was active and saw 122.9 million shares traded, although 44.7 million of these were in debut listing Popular Holdings, which went to lunch at Singapore $0.510 against an offer price of S$0.36.
Vickers Ballas shares stood at S$1.25 after the impact of a one-for-one bonus issue.
Gainers were led by Creative Technology, up S$2.30 at S$28.50, easing back from an all-time high of S$28.80.
Bank stocks rebounded after Thursday's falls with DBS Bank foreign shares leading the charge, up S$0.50 at S$18.30.
